subject: Co-term signal and pricing safety net
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novacare.com>
To: elliot_price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@novacare.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Increased usage this quarter — options for midterm top-up and co-term

Hi Elliot,

Quick note from our side: usage spiked ~45% this month due to a pilot we kicked off. We expect the elevated token usage to persist through Q3 unless we dial back features. Finance asked whether we can do a midterm top-up (temporary committed capacity) and also align our renewal to the existing annual date (co-term) so we don’t have two overlapping invoices next year.

Can Redwood provision a short-term uplift that gives us headroom and a pricing "safety net" — something like an interim committed bucket with a refundable or credit-backed buffer if usage normalizes? Also, we need to understand how co-terming would be handled (true up, proration, and whether there are discounts for consolidating early).

Attachments: Novacare_MAU_report_Q2.pdf (summary of spike by product)

Would appreciate a proposal by Friday so we can brief procurement. Happy to set a quick 30m call.

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of Platform Operations
Novacare Health

--
ops@novacare.com (shared mailbox)

From: elliot_price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novacare.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased usage this quarter — options for midterm top-up and co-term

Hi Samantha — thanks for the heads up and the MAU report. Congrats on the pilot traction.

Summary of options we can move quickly on (we can put any of these into a short amendment + SOW):

1) Temporary top-up (30–90 days)
  - Add a provisional committed bucket (example: +500k tokens/mo) at a blended uplift price of 12% above your current rate.
  - If actual usage for the top-up period ends up below the provisional bucket, we can convert the difference to a credit applied to the next invoice ("fallthrough credit").

2) Short-term credit buffer (no committed spend)
  - We reserve capacity for you; if you exceed baseline we bill incremental usage at a capped rate and issue a one-time rebate if usage drops below baseline within 60 days.

3) Co-term alignment + proration approach
  - When you opt to co-term, we pro-rate the remaining annual commitment and either annualize at current rates or offer a tiered consolidation discount (sliding scale 5–12% depending on annualized commit).
  - One-time co-term fee waiver available for existing Enterprise customers in the US who sign the amendment inside 30 days.

Next steps I propose: 1) quick call to confirm expected uplift magnitude and preferred protection (provisional bucket vs buffer), 2) we model the pro-forma invoice and co-term proration, 3) draft a narrow amendment for signatures.

If that works, how’s 1:00pm PT today or 9:30am PT tomorrow for a 30m?

Best,
Elliot
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Draft-Amendment-v2.docx (template amendment for top-up + co-term)

Subject: Internal: Novacare — pricing approach

Elliot / Priyom — quick internal guidance before the call:

- We should favor a provisional bucket with fallthrough credit vs a pure buffer for enterprise customers; it preserves committed revenue while giving the customer confidence.
- Suggested concession: cap the uplift to 10% for the first 2 months, then revisit. If they agree to annualize (co-term) we layer a 6% consolidation discount at $X annualized commit.
- Require finance sign-off on any refundable credit language — avoid language that looks like a refund; prefer "invoice credit" applied to future usage.
- Legal wants the amendment to include a clause that automatic throttling is the fallback if we hit capacity limits (to protect other customers).

I'll join the call and can bring a quick proration calculator. Marcus — if procurement pushes for credits instead of proration, can you escalate a 1-off credit approval ($Y max)?

Thanks,
Laura
Head of Renewals Operations
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novacare.com>, elliot_price <elliot.price@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased usage this quarter — options for midterm top-up and co-term

Samantha — just following up from our call. Good to hear use case detail. From Finance: we can approve a provisional + fallthrough credit path. Key terms we will put in the amendment:

- Term: 60-day provisional top-up of 600k tokens/mo at +10% uplift.
- Fallthrough: unused provisional tokens convert to invoice credit applied to next billing cycle. No cash refunds.
- Co-term: if Novacare elects to annualize within 30 days, we will apply a consolidated discount of 6% on the annualized incremental commit and waive the co-term processing fee.
- Approval: Marcus Lin (Finance) approves up to $75k in one-off credit conversion authority for this amendment. Anything beyond requires VP approval.

I've attached the amended draft for signatures and included a DocuSign link in the HubSpot record. Please review and let me know if procurement needs a slightly different structure.

Attachments: Draft-Amendment-v2.docx
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/987654/DEAL-9987 (DocuSign envelope attached)

Thanks,
Marcus
